cards.title: Notch calculator: RATING_SCALE, notchChange, notchCalculator (src/ratings/notch.mjs)
cards.context:
WHY: REQ-06-02. Other Watchlist POC modules need a shared helper that takes a previous and a current rating and returns the notch change, the direction and the resulting WL (Watchlist level, 0-4, higher is worse). Card T-02 (Indicator 12) depends on this module, so it goes first. The repo is empty apart from package.json (type module, script `npm test`), src/.gitkeep and test/.gitkeep.

STACK / CONVENTIONS (CLAUDE.md): plain Node.js 18+ ES modules (.mjs). No npm dependencies; do not add any, and do not add dependencies/devDependencies to package.json. No APIs newer than Node 18. src/ratings holds pure functions only: no I/O, no imports of node:fs, node:http or any other I/O module, no console/stdout/stderr output, no logging, no state. Tests use node:test with node:assert/strict. Work TDD.

FILES: create src/ratings/notch.mjs and test/ratings/notch.test.mjs. Touch nothing else.

CONTRACT (export names are fixed; other POC parts import them):
1. `export const RATING_SCALE` is a frozen array (Object.freeze) of exactly these 19 strings, best first: ['AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-']. Object.isFrozen is true; in strict mode RATING_SCALE.push('D') throws TypeError and the length stays 19.
2. `export function notchChange(previous, current)` returns index(current) - index(previous), an integer from -18 to +18. Positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 = unchanged.
3. `export function notchCalculator(previous, current)` returns an object with exactly the keys { notches, direction, wl }: notches === notchChange(previous, current) (C5); direction is 'downgrade' when notches > 0, 'upgrade' when < 0, 'unchanged' when 0; wl uses the INDICATOR 13 thresholds (C2, C6): 0 when notches <= 1 (all upgrades/unchanged included), 1 when notches is exactly 2, 2 when notches >= 3. Derive notches from notchChange so the two cannot drift apart.

INPUT NORMALISATION (binding X-input-trim): String.prototype.trim() on each argument, then toUpperCase(), then look up in RATING_SCALE. Internal whitespace is not removed, so 'BBB +' is invalid.

ERRORS (binding CON-errors, X-error-message, X-scale-bounds): all exported functions throw RangeError (never TypeError) when an argument is not one of the 19 ratings after trim and upper-case. Check type-safely so non-strings (null, undefined, numbers, objects, arrays such as ['BBB']) also throw RangeError instead of crashing on .trim(). Must reject: '', '   ', 'BBB +', 'BBB\u2212', CC, C, D, SD, RD, NR, Baa1, AAA+. Check `previous` first, then `current`. The message names the argument ('previous' or 'current') and echoes the value, e.g. notchChange('XX','YY') message contains 'previous' and 'XX'; notchChange('BBB','YY') contains 'current' and 'YY'. No fallback, default WL or partial result. Put validation and index lookup in one internal helper (T-02 reuses notchChange and must not repeat it).

JSDoc: document every export. The notchCalculator JSDoc must say wl uses the Indicator 13 thresholds (<=1 -> 0, 2 -> 1, >=3 -> 2) and that this differs on purpose from Indicator 12 (countryRatingChangeWl), which gives 1 for a 1-notch downgrade (C6). Document the sign convention and the RangeError.

KNOWN TRAP: the POC example 'BBB+ -> BB+ = 2 notches, WL=1' is wrong. Per C2 it is 3 notches, WL 2. No test may assert the literal POC example.

OUT OF SCOPE: Indicator 13 as an indicator (no externalRatingChangeWl export), override parameter, persistence, audit trail, UI/CLI output, fetching ratings from a public source, ratings outside the scale (they throw).
acceptance: AC-1: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then `RATING_SCALE` deep-equals ["AAA","AA+","AA","AA-","A+","A","A-","BBB+","BBB","BBB-","BB+","BB","BB-","B+","B","B-","CCC+","CCC","CCC-"]; length 19; [0] "AAA"; [18] "CCC-"; `Object.isFrozen` true.

AC-1: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then In a strict-mode (ESM) test `RATING_SCALE.push("D")` throws TypeError and length stays 19; `RATING_SCALE[0] = "X"` throws TypeError and [0] stays "AAA".

AC-2: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then `notchChange` = index(current) − index(previous): ("BBB+","BB+")=3, ("BBB+","BBB-")=2, ("BBB+","BBB")=1, ("AA","AA")=0, ("BB+","BBB+")=-3, ("AAA","CCC-")=18, ("CCC-","AAA")=-18.
AC-2: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then For any two valid ratings the result is an integer in −18..+18; positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 = unchanged.

AC-3: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then `notchCalculator` deepStrictEquals: ("BBB+","BB+") {notches:3,direction:"downgrade",wl:2}; ("BBB+","BBB-") {2,"downgrade",1}; ("BBB+","BBB") {1,"downgrade",0}; ("AAA","CCC-") {18,"downgrade",2}.
AC-3: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then No test asserts `notches: 2` or `wl: 1` for ("BBB+","BB+") (the POC example is wrong; C2 says 3 notches, WL 2).

AC-4: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then ("BB+","BBB+") {-3,"upgrade",0}; ("BBB","BBB+") {-1,"upgrade",0}; ("CCC-","AAA") {-18,"upgrade",0}; ("AA","AA") {0,"unchanged",0}.

AC-5: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then For all 361 ordered pairs from RATING_SCALE × RATING_SCALE: `notches === notchChange(p,c)`; direction "downgrade"/"upgrade"/"unchanged" for >0/<0/0; wl 0 if notches<=1, 1 if 2, 2 if >=3; `Object.keys(r).sort()` equals ["direction","notches","wl"]. Control totals: downgrade 171, upgrade 171, unchanged 19; wl0 208, wl1 17, wl2 136.

AC-8: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then `notchChange(" bbb+ ","Bb+")===3`; `notchChange("aaa","ccc-")===18`; `notchCalculator("\tbbb+\n","bbb-")` deep-equals {notches:2,direction:"downgrade",wl:1}. Normalisation = trim() then toUpperCase().

AC-9: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then For each V in "", "   ", "BBB +", "BBB−", "CC", "C", "D", "SD", "RD", "NR", "Baa1", "AAA+", null, undefined, 7, {}, ["BBB"]: `notchChange(V,"BBB")`, `notchChange("BBB",V)`, `notchCalculator(V,"BBB")`, `notchCalculator("BBB",V)` each throw `RangeError` (`assert.throws(fn, RangeError)`), never TypeError.

AC-10: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then `notchChange("XX","YY")` throws RangeError whose message contains "previous" and "XX"; `notchChange("BBB","YY")` message contains "current" and "YY"; `notchCalculator` reports the same way.
AC-11: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then Same arguments twice give deepStrictEqual results (each a new object); no state kept.

AC-11: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then A child process importing the module and calling the functions (including a caught RangeError) has empty stdout/stderr and exit 0; the source of `src/ratings/notch.mjs` has no `import`/`require` statements and no `console.`, `process.stdout`, `process.stderr`.

AC-12: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then `node --test` reports 0 failures; both files exist and use ESM `export` (no `module.exports`); `package.json` has no `dependencies`/`devDependencies` and is unchanged from main.

cards.title: Indicator 12 country rating change WL: countryRatingChangeWl (src/indicators/countryRating.mjs)
cards.context:
WHY: REQ-03-12. Indicator 12 (country rating change) gives a WL (Watchlist level, higher is worse) worked out from the notch change between a country's previous and current rating. It builds on card T-01, so it starts after T-01 is merged into the job branch.

STACK / CONVENTIONS (CLAUDE.md): plain Node.js 18+ ES modules (.mjs). No npm dependencies; do not add any. No APIs newer than Node 18. src/indicators holds pure functions only: no I/O, no imports of node:fs, node:http or any other I/O module, no console/stdout/stderr output, no logging, no state. Tests use node:test with node:assert/strict. Work TDD.

FILES: create src/indicators/countryRating.mjs and test/indicators/countryRating.test.mjs. Do NOT edit src/ratings/notch.mjs (owned by T-01); if it looks wrong, raise it under Open issues.

DEPENDENCY (from T-01, in place): src/ratings/notch.mjs exports RATING_SCALE (frozen array of 19 ratings, AAA index 0 .. CCC- index 18), notchChange(previous, current) (index(current) - index(previous), positive = downgrade) and notchCalculator(previous, current) ({notches, direction, wl}, Indicator 13 thresholds). notchChange already does normalisation and validation: trim() then toUpperCase(); RangeError (never TypeError) for anything not one of the 19 ratings, non-strings included; `previous` checked first, message names the argument and echoes the value.

CONTRACT (name is fixed; other POC parts import it): `export function countryRatingChangeWl(previous, current)` returns 0 | 1 | 2. It MUST import with exactly `import { notchChange } from '../ratings/notch.mjs';` and compute n = notchChange(previous, current). Then: 0 when n <= 0 (an upgrade or unchanged never raises the WL, C3); 1 when n === 1; 2 when n >= 2. Do not re-implement the scale, normalisation or validation. Let notchChange's RangeError pass through unchanged.

THRESHOLDS DIFFER ON PURPOSE (C6): for a 1-notch downgrade such as (BBB+,BBB), countryRatingChangeWl returns 1, but notchCalculator returns wl 0 (Indicator 13: <=1 -> 0, 2 -> 1, >=3 -> 2). The JSDoc on countryRatingChangeWl must name its thresholds (Indicator 12: <=0 -> 0, 1 -> 1, >=2 -> 2), point out this difference from notchCalculator, and document the RangeError. Add a unit test showing the difference for (BBB+,BBB).

OUT OF SCOPE: override parameter, persistence, audit trail, fetching ratings from a public source, UI/CLI output, Indicator 13 as an indicator, SD/RD/NR or other ratings outside the scale (they throw RangeError; recorded risk).
acceptance: AC-6: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then `countryRatingChangeWl("A","A-")===1`, `("BBB+","BBB")===1`, `("A","BBB+")===2`, `("BBB+","BB+")===2`, `("AAA","CCC-")===2`.

AC-6: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then `countryRatingChangeWl("BBB+","BBB")===1` while `notchCalculator("BBB+","BBB").wl===0`; intended (C6), asserted in `test/indicators/countryRating.test.mjs`.
AC-7: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then `("BBB","BBB+")===0`, `("BB+","BBB+")===0`, `("CCC-","AAA")===0`, `("AA","AA")===0`.

AC-7: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then For all 361 ordered pairs from RATING_SCALE × RATING_SCALE with n = notchChange(p,c): result 0 if n<=0, 1 if n===1, 2 if n>=2; always a number 0/1/2. Control totals: 0 → 190, 1 → 18, 2 → 153.
AC-8: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then `countryRatingChangeWl("a"," A- ")===1`.

AC-9: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then For each V in "", "   ", "BBB +", "BBB−", "CC", "C", "D", "SD", "RD", "NR", "Baa1", "AAA+", null, undefined, 7, {}, ["BBB"]: `countryRatingChangeWl(V,"BBB")` and `countryRatingChangeWl("BBB",V)` throw RangeError (never TypeError).

AC-9 / X-error-message: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then `countryRatingChangeWl("XX","YY")` message contains "previous" and "XX"; `("BBB","YY")` contains "current" and "YY"; the error passes through unchanged from `notchChange` (not caught, wrapped or re-thrown).

AC-11: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then Repeated calls with the same arguments return the same value; `("A","A-")` → 1 then `("A","BBB+")` → 2 (analyst-edited rating just changes the result); nothing left behind.

AC-11: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then A child process importing the module and calling it (including a caught RangeError) has empty stdout/stderr and exit 0; the source's only import is from '../ratings/notch.mjs' — no fs/http/net/child_process; no `console.`, `process.stdout`, `process.stderr`.

AC-12: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then The source contains `import { notchChange } from '../ratings/notch.mjs';` and exports `countryRatingChangeWl` with ESM syntax; it does not repeat the scale (no literal rating list such as "AAA"/"CCC-") and has no trim/toUpperCase normalisation.

AC-12: Given the exports as specified, when called with the data below, then With T-01 merged, `node --test` reports 0 failures including `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs`; `package.json` has no `dependencies`/`devDependencies`; `src/ratings/notch.mjs` is unchanged by this card.
